text:
Nick DeSimone is the kind of defenseman every injury-hit team needs: an undrafted 31-year-old who has bounced between Calgary, New Jersey and Utah, and who CBS Sports notes is playing regularly as a fill-in. He's dressed for eight games this season, about 14 minutes a night, without a point.

The small sample says he's held up. Utah takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with DeSimone on the ice, roughly the team rate, and 55% of the shot attempts. The Mammoth have scored a couple of goals fewer than the chances deserve during his shifts, which is why the points column is empty.

Last season, Evolving-Hockey rated him a useful depth piece, 76th of 215 defensemen, with 89th-percentile defensive impact. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, showed a defenseman who carries the puck into the zone half the time but keeps possession on only 26% of his exits, so watch for clears off the glass under pressure. Our talent range has him around 11 points if he keeps playing. With Nate Schmidt out, he will for now.
